comment: Sustaining a high-performing digital public infrastructure requires continuous, long-term operational funding to prevent system drift. This funding is only politically and economically defensible if it is mathematically justified by the avoidance of high-cost clinical complications. Treating operational maintenance as an isolated IT cost center makes infrastructure vulnerable to budget cuts that trigger technical decay.

public.text: Sustaining a high-performing digital public infrastructure requires continuous, long-term operational funding to prevent system drift. This funding is only politically and economically defensible if it is mathematically justified by the avoidance of high-cost clinical complications. Treating operational maintenance as an isolated IT cost center makes infrastructure vulnerable to budget cuts that trigger technical decay.
public.suggestedRevision: Add to investment case guidance: “Guidelines should instruct member states to explicitly link recurring operational IT maintenance budgets to the clinical-economic savings realized through coordinated chronic disease management. Rather than treating maintenance as an isolated IT expense, the operational business case should demonstrate how closed clinical loops prevent high-cost disease endpoints—such as avoiding costly dialysis regimens through early-stage glycemic and blood pressure control.”
